fields.meta_title: Restaurant Reservation Form With Cover Limits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a restaurant reservation form that caps covers per seating, routes big parties to private dining and saves bookings to your database.
fields.h1: Build a Restaurant Reservation Form That Counts Every Cover
fields.hero_description: Tell Emergent how many guests each seating takes. It builds a restaurant reservation form that checks each party against the room left and saves bookings to your own table.
fields.features_heading: Made for Seatings, Not Calendar Slots
fields.features_subheading: A dining room sells seats in waves. These six parts keep each booking inside what the floor and the kitchen can serve.
fields.feature_1:
Covers capped per seating

Set how many guests each 15-minute seating can take, night by night. A party that would push a seating past its cap sees the nearest times that still have room for everyone.
fields.feature_2:
Party size limits

Choose how many guests the form books on its own. Bigger groups get a private dining request instead, with the room's minimum spend shown before they send it in for approval.
fields.feature_3:
Deposits for large groups

Take a flat or per-guest deposit through Stripe or any processor with an API. A large-party request becomes a booking once the deposit clears and the events manager approves it.
fields.feature_4:
Allergy and dietary notes

List the major food allergens as checkboxes, then add a note field for anything else. Every flag prints on the night's reservation sheet beside its table number and seat time.
fields.feature_5:
Confirmations and reminders

Send a confirmation when a table is booked and a reminder a day ahead, each with a link to cancel. Your no-show terms appear in plain words in both, right above the cancel link.
fields.feature_6:
On your site, in your repo

Publish the form on the restaurant's own domain or put it behind the Reserve button on the site you run now. Export the full code to GitHub when a developer wants to extend it.
fields.why_title: Why Build Reservation Forms With Emergent?

fields.usecase_heading: Booking Rules From Four Dining Rooms
fields.tab_content_1:
16 covers a seating, with 7:15 or 7:45 next

Larder Bistro seats 52 and takes 16 covers in each 15-minute seating, a pace its kitchen can plate. A party of four asks for 7:30, where 14 covers are already booked. The form offers 7:15, with 7 covers left, or 7:45, with 6. The host sees the booking land on tonight's sheet.
fields.tab_content_2:
Over eight guests, it becomes a private dining request

Any party over eight at Casa Olmo skips the table picker. A request for 12 on Friday goes to the private dining room, which seats 24 and carries a $1,500 food-and-beverage minimum. The guest pays a $300 deposit through Stripe, and the events manager gets the request in Slack to approve.
fields.tab_content_3:
Allergies by table number, in the kitchen at 4 pm

Every booking at Kinto Ramen asks about the nine major food allergens, with a box for anything else. At 4 pm the kitchen channel in Slack gets tonight's flagged tables with their seat times. Table 6 at 6:00 tops the list with a sesame allergy.
fields.tab_content_4:
Tables freed when guests cancel go to the waitlist

Quill Wine Bar emails every guest 24 hours ahead with Confirm and Cancel buttons. When a four-top for 8:00 cancels, those covers go back into the seating. The next waitlist party that fits gets an email offering the table, and the offer holds for 20 minutes before it moves down the list.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Restaurant Reservation Form
fields.howto_description: Start from what the kitchen can serve in each seating. The form only asks what those limits need to know.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Count the covers you can serve
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Draw the line for large parties
fields.howto_step_1_des: A cover is one guest: a table of four counts as four covers. Write how many covers each seating can take on each night, such as 16 every 15 minutes on Fridays. Note the first and last seating times too.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the party size where online booking stops. Above it, send the request to a private room or a set menu, and note the minimum spend and deposit for each. A host can still seat a big walk-in by hand.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Say how long a late table is held and whether large groups pay a fee for not showing up. Keep it to two short sentences, because the terms print in every confirmation and reminder the guest receives.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for the essentials first: when, how many, and a name with a phone number. Add allergies or a high chair only if the floor uses them. Drop any field the host never reads, since guests fill it in on a phone.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the dining room to Emergent
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the seating caps and party limits into the prompt, with the no-show terms last. Emergent builds the form and its bookings table, plus the confirmation emails. Change any rule by asking, such as moving the last Friday seating to 9:45.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Make a booking under a made-up name. Then try the cases a paper book handles badly: four guests into a nearly full seating, a group of nine, a sesame allergy and a cancellation with a waitlist party ready.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put the link where diners look
fields.howto_step_7_des: Link the form from the restaurant's website and its Instagram bio, and paste it into replies to email inquiries. A QR code on the check presenter lets guests book a return visit before they leave.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is printable sheets and PDFs (Pinterest, SampleForms, Scribd, pdfFiller), template galleries (Ninja Forms, Jotform, Form81) and a PHP tutorial. Every one hands over name, date, time and party size, and none knows how many covers the kitchen can take at 7:30. This page is for restaurants that want a reservation form on their own site instead of a paper book: it shows the form checking covers per seating, sending large parties to a private dining request with a deposit, carrying allergy notes to the kitchen and releasing canceled tables to the waitlist, all in a database the restaurant owns. Rooms and nights stay with the hotel sibling and generic slot holds with the booking form sibling; the FAQ answers the diner-side PAA from the host stand.
tab_stories: A 52-seat bistro caps every 15-minute seating at 16 covers, so a party of four asking for 7:30 when 14 covers are booked is offered 7:15 or 7:45 instead.

A trattoria sends any party over eight to its private dining room request, which carries a $1,500 food-and-beverage minimum and a $300 deposit paid through Stripe before the events manager confirms it.
A ramen bar asks every booking for allergies against the nine major food allergens, and at 4 pm the kitchen gets one list of the night's flagged tables with seat times.
A wine bar sends a confirm-or-cancel email 24 hours ahead, and when a four-top cancels, the covers return to that seating and the first waitlist party that fits gets 20 minutes to claim the table.
